card.intuition: A model provider is whatever serves a model for inference — usually a remote service like Anthropic or OpenAI, but it can be local via Ollama or llama.cpp. The provider owns the machinery: parameters live on its hardware, which makes it the source of rate limits, degraded capacity, and outages. It also sets the commercial terms: per-token pricing and prefix-cache discounts.
card.analogy: A rented GPU cluster with a service contract: you don't own the compute, the vendor's status page is your first stop when things stall, and the meter is the vendor's own.
card.time_complexity: Every model provider request is a network round-trip plus inference on the provider's hardware; rate limits and degraded capacity surface as stalls in the agent loop, while local providers trade capability for zero marginal cost.
card.space_complexity: Parameters live on provider hardware, so the session's context footprint still travels over the network as tokens on each request — only a local provider keeps it on your machine.
when_to_use: Swapping providers (remote to local) for an air-gapped client — the harness just hits a different endpoint
Checking the provider status page before anything else when an agent stalls or errors on every turn
Comparing per-token pricing, prefix-cache discounts, and model availability across providers
gotchas: Rate limits, capacity, and outages are provider problems that get misattributed to the model or harness
The provider and the model's maker can differ — Bedrock, Vertex, and OpenRouter serve other companies' models

steps.label: Harness asks
steps.annotation: The harness sends tokens over the network to the provider.

steps.label: Provider runs
steps.annotation: The provider runs the model on its own hardware.

steps.label: Returns
steps.annotation: Predictions come back to the harness.

steps.label: Bills
steps.annotation: The provider bills input and output tokens plus cache discounts.

steps.label: Status
steps.annotation: Provider failures surface as stalls and errors in the agent loop.
